question: Who holds power in NEAR’s House of Stake? Make me a fresh flower, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with the signature each completion got. A hash or link the model copied from a tool result is written as a reference to that result ($from, {{…}}), so it replays on recordedClient.

turns.content: I'll start by finding the network.

interpretation.summary: Petal read NEAR's House of Stake at final block 223167645 (2026-11-05). Each petal is a veNEAR account; its width and height show its share of the 5,364,610.01 veNEAR of voting power, largest first clockwise. Power is highly concentrated: the top 5 accounts hold 50.7% and the top 10 hold 81.1%. 519 participants were read, of which 465 hold measurable voting power.

power_means.claim: Power in the House of Stake is veNEAR voting power: own locked NEAR grown by lock time, minus delegations out, plus delegations in.
Five accounts suffice to pass a 50% threshold; the top 10 hold 81.1% of voting power.
The distribution is extremely unequal, with a long tail of 405 accounts holding 0.014% between them.

mappings.why: Share of veNEAR voting power, compressed into a band; the largest holder has 15.3%.
Square root of the same share, so mid-sized holders stay visible beside the top.
Named (human-readable account id) versus anonymous (implicit account), so you can see who is identifiable at all.
Solid where a name is self-declared, none where unknown; no identity here is proven.
Most voting power first, clockwise from the top.

conflicts: Legal or organisational power, reputation and off-chain influence in NEAR governance are not drawn; only on-chain veNEAR voting power is.
The two largest holders are implicit accounts (anonymous), so their real-world standing cannot be shown.
unknowns: Addresses are not people: several accounts may belong to one person, and delegations already move power between them, but common control is not read.
Per-voter votes on the 30 proposals are not read, so actual voting behaviour is unknown.
Each holder's lockup contract and its staking, and off-chain delegate profiles, are not included.
Whether a name is a verified identity: all names here are self-declared account ids.
inferred: The top holders are likely delegates or organisations accumulating delegated veNEAR, but this is not checked per account.

**What you'll see**: 60 petals, one per veNEAR account, largest voting power first clockwise, with the remaining 405 accounts hatched together as "everyone else" (<0.1%).

- Width & height — each account's share of veNEAR voting power (total 5,364,610.01 veNEAR); width log-banded, height √ (source: `venear-accounts`, `hos-source`).
- Colour — named account id vs anonymous implicit account; outline solid where the name is self-declared (`account-id`).
- Order — most power first (`venear-accounts`).

**Changed from the default**: colour, set to identity.

**The numbers**: top 1 holds 15.3%, top 5 hold 50.7%, top 10 hold 81.1%; Nakamoto coefficient at 50% is 5; Gini 0.976, HHI 0.084. 465 of 519 participants carry measurable power.

**What this can't tell you**: addresses aren't people — common control isn't read; per-voter votes on the 30 proposals aren't read; lockup contracts and off-chain delegate profiles aren't included; every name is self-declared, never proven. Legal, reputational and off-chain influence isn't drawn — only on-chain veNEAR.
